headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared filesystem/repo context; Copilot Workspace edits can amplify AutoGPT outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs, while GitHub Copilot reads editor open buffers and repo context. That shared file-based bridge lets attacker-controlled content in AutoGPT outputs be interpreted by Copilot as instructions in default workflows, even without MCP. The interaction is plausible but not proven beyond docs.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes prompt-like text into files that Copilot ingests as repo context
IF Copilot Workspace or chat treats file contents as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to a separate repo copy
Add a prompt-injection banner to AutoGPT-generated files
Require human review before Copilot consumes AutoGPT outputs
Use allowlisted file paths only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress; Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, both agents can access them and Copilot may transmit context to a third-party service. The profiles do not show secrets handling or isolation strong enough to lower this.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared repo or workspace
IF Copilot context includes those files during chat or Workspace use
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a redacted test repository
Disable Copilot on sensitive directories
Review editor buffers before invoking Copilot
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while Copilot can write files and modify git state. Even though Copilot is editor-scoped and AutoGPT lacks explicit git-write capability, both can mutate the same repository contents, creating overlapping writes and race-prone edits in default collaborative use. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree
IF AutoGPT shell actions and Copilot edits occur without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent while the other writes
Review git diff before merge
Use file-level locks for shared paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace can propose and apply edits from context, and AutoGPT can generate outputs that may be treated as task input. That creates a default pathway where Copilot may act on AutoGPT-produced text without a verification step. The profiles do not prove autonomous downstream execution, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is pasted or indexed into Copilot context
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits based on that context without human verification
mitigations: Require a second human review step
Keep AutoGPT outputs in a separate notes file
Use explicit source labels in prompts
Compare proposed edits against original intent
requires-engineering: add verification gates before apply

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo-context access, while AutoGPT is open-source and locally runnable with filesystem access. The profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or a residency mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is evidenced: differing retention and processing boundaries may matter if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository or editor buffers
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to a vendor AI service
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use synthetic fixtures
Review vendor terms and retention settings
Limit Copilot to non-sensitive repos
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
